title: Compass QBR deck + renewal tracker (concise standard + enterprise variants)
content:
Purpose: Provide a compact, repeatable QBR deck and an accompanying renewal tracker that CS managers can adapt quickly for both Standard and Enterprise customers. Keep the deck 10-14 slides for exec + product-focused QBRs; include appendices for technical deep-dive and contract/Risk details.

Audience: Customer Success Managers, Account Execs, Solutions Engineers, and Customer stakeholders (Owners, Eng leads, Procurement).

Design principles / notes to self:
- One-page executive summary up front: health summary + renewal ask + 1-3 wins + 1 risk.
- Use a clean 2-column layout for metrics slides to avoid slide bloat.
- Two flavors: Standard (concise, metrics-first) and Enterprise (narrative + roadmap alignment + risk mitigation).
- Always include: last 90d usage trend, latency/cost anomalies (if customer on Redwood Dedicated/Private), feature adoption, NPS/CSAT snapshot, Q3 product roadmap items that matter to customer.
- Leave clear CTAs: decision needed, proposed renewal options, point person, timeline.

Slide-by-slide outline (Master):
1) Cover / Meeting Info (title, customer name, date, attendees, owner) - 30s opener
2) Executive summary (1 box each: Health: GREEN/AMBER/RED; Renewal window + ask; Top 3 wins; Top 1-2 risks) - 2 mins
3) Health metrics dashboard (utilization, latency p50/p95, error rate, token cost delta vs baseline) - 3 mins
4) Adoption & usage (active apps, endpoints, percent of requests using caching/batching, model variants in use) - 2 mins
5) Business impact / outcomes (cases where LLM features moved KPIs: CTR, time saved, conversion lift) - 2 mins
6) Product roadmap alignment (items shipping next 90-180d relevant to customer; shipping date confidence) - 2 mins (Enterprise: expand to 2 slides)
7) Support & reliability (SLA adherence, incident recap last quarter, SRE action plan) - 2 mins
8) Cost posture & optimization opportunities (quantization, batching, routing policy changes to lower unit costs) - 2 mins
9) Renewal options & recommended path (Standard: 12-month renewal options; Enterprise: tiered commitments + professional services + SLOs) - 3 mins
10) Risk register & mitigation plan (top 3 risks, owners, due dates) - 2 mins
11) Ask / decision & next steps (clear dates + owners + follow-up cadence) - 1 min
12) Appendix: Technical deep dive / logs (for SEs), Contract summary (for AE), full incident timeline (SRE) - use only if needed

Standard variant guidance (concise):
- Limit to slides 1-5 + 9-11; move other items to appendix.
- Emphasize usage trends and direct business metrics.
- Use 2 renewal options: auto-renew with 10% usage discount OR 12-month prepay with X% off.
- Single owner CTA: "CS Manager + AE" with date for renewal decision.

Enterprise variant guidance (expanded):
- Add a dedicated roadmap alignment slide and a customer-specific migration/latency optimization plan.
- Include a separate slide for Legal/compliance notes (if private deployment).
- Offer tiered SLAs, dedicated on-call hours, quarterly architecture reviews, and optional professional services block.
- Provide a sample rollout timeline for Dedicated/Private migration (if relevant).

Renewal tracker template (simple table described for copy/paste into sheet):
Columns: Customer | ARR (current) | Renewal window start | Renewal window end | Proposed option | CS owner | AE owner | Contract signed? | Notes | Risk (L/M/H) | Next action date
Notes: keep one row per document; color code Risk. Keep a filtered view for >60-day renewals.

Conversation scripts / talking points (short):
- Exec summary: "In the last quarter you've seen X% increase in request volume with p95 latency held at Yms and costs flat/within expectations. We recommend option A to lock pricing and add dedicated on-call hours to reduce mean time to diagnose."
- When risk = AMBER: "We observed a recurring error pattern on endpoint /chat. We've deployed a mitigation (kv-cache increase) and propose a joint runbook and a canary rollout for the next model update."
- Pricing negotiation fallback: "If the customer cannot commit to annual at this time, propose a 6-month pilot with 90-day review and measured SLAs. Outline exit criteria clearly."

One-page renewal email templates (short drafts):
- Initial renewal outreach (CS -> Exec): "Hi <Name>, hope all is well — as your renewal window approaches, we'd like to propose options and schedule a 20-30m QBR to review impact and next steps. Proposed dates: <dates>. Attached: concise summary. Best, <CS>"
- Post-QBR decision follow-up: "Thanks for meeting. Per our conversation, we will: 1) send formal quote for Option A by <date>; 2) schedule architecture review on <date>. Owner: <AE>. Please confirm."

Risk playbook quick reference (bullets):
- RED (immediate): open exec escalations + 48h action plan + on-call remediation + AE engaged.
- AMBER: weekly checkpoints, technical deep-dive, targeted optimizations.
- GREEN: quarterly reviews + proactive suggestions.

Appendix content ideas (copy into slide notes):
- How we measure health score: weighted metrics (usage trend 30%, latency 20%, error rate 20%, feature adoption 20%, CSAT/NPS 10%) — thresholds: >70 GREEN, 40-70 AMBER, <40 RED. (Note: weights draft, invite product to confirm)
- Defensive language for public pricing vs enterprise pricing negotiation.
- Quick checklist for SRE/SE before QBR: collect p95 by region, export top 10 error traces, confirm incident postmortem links.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Add sample numeric badges for "health score" visualization — Marcus to prototype.
- Decide on final discount ranges for Standard offers (legal needs to sign off).
- Lina to provide 3 anonymized customer ROI examples for the business impact slide.
- Confirm template font and brand colors with Marketing (Sophie).

Usage guidance for CS managers:
- Keep slides lightweight in customer-facing copy. Use appendix for any logs or sensitive items.
- Share deck 48h before QBR with customer; include draft agenda and desired outcomes.
- Follow-up: send meeting notes and update the renewal tracker (assign next action).

Sample short meeting agenda (20-30m):
- 0-3m: Introductions + agenda
- 3-7m: Exec summary + decision ask
- 7-15m: Health + adoption + roadmap alignment
- 15-22m: Renewal options + risk discussion
- 22-30m: Decisions + next steps

Distribution & ownership notes:
- Template stored in Drive: /customer-success/Compass QBR kit (this doc).
- For enterprise renewals, copy deck and tag AE + Solutions Eng in a Slack thread and link to Tracker row.
- CS manager is responsible to update tracker row within 48h of QBR.

Quick change log (for internal):
- 2025-01-10: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-01-22: added Enterprise variant language and renewal table (Marcus)
- 2025-02-02: inserted sample email copy and TODOs (Lina)

End notes (informal):
- This is intentionally concise — if a customer wants a deeper technical review, spin up the appendix slides and schedule a separate 60m architecture session.
- Would like to get CSM feedback after 3 pilot QBRs to refine slide counts and health scoring weights.

-- Aisha (draft)
